notes.decision: Coptic numeral 77 (ⲟ=70, ⲍ=7). Standalone on its own line as the chapter-marker preceding the full chapter heading. Standard Manichaean Kephalaia layout for chapter divisions.
Read as ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ-(ⲡ)ϥⲧⲟⲉ 'of the four' with assimilation. ϥⲧⲟⲉ is Lyc variant of ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ '4.' Together with following ⲙ̄ⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲟ gives 'of the four kingdoms.'

Translated 'the land of Babylon and the Persian land' as the first member of the standard Manichaean four-kingdoms enumeration. Babylon-Persia is treated as a single political-cosmographic unit (the Sasanian heartland, Mani's own context). The four kingdoms are: (1) Babylon-Persia, (2) Romans, (3) Aksumites, (4) Sileus/Silīs (Eastern empire, often China). This mirrors known Manichaean cosmographic-imperial doctrine.

Restored as 'Aksumites' based on the standard four-kingdoms list. The form ⲛⲉϩⲟⲙⲧⲏⲥ may reflect a corrupted/Lycopolitan rendering of Ἀξωμῖται (Aksumites). Confidence is moderate-high based on the position in the canonical four-kingdom list rather than direct philological reading.

Preserved transliterated 'Sileus' for the fourth kingdom, identified in Manichaean cosmography with the eastern empire (Silīs, often understood as China or the Land of Silk). Capitalized as proper name.
Translated 'there is none exalted exceedingly above them' — closing line of the four-kingdoms summary. The leer that follows marks a major section break before the new teaching on hospitality.

notes.coptic_form: ⲁⲛⲁⲕ ⲇⲉ ⲧⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ ⲁⲣⲱⲧⲛ ⲍⲛ ⲟⲩⲙⲏⲉ
notes.decision: Standard Manichaean teacher-formula 'But I, I say it to you in truth' — opens the new section that contrasts the four worldly kingdoms with the surpassing reward for hospitality to disciples and catechumens. Echoes Synoptic ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν.

Tentatively rendered 'shall live (before God)' from ⲱⲛⲉϩ 'live' (cf. ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'eternity' on this page). Could alternatively be from ⲱϩⲉ 'stand,' giving 'shall stand before God' — both fit eschatological-reward context. Translation preserves verbal aspect either way.

Tentatively translated 'being led inward' — ⲧⲍⲛⲁⲓ̈ⲧ appears to be a passive/relative verbal form on a stem of guiding/bringing, with ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' specifying spatial direction. The catechumen who hosts a disciple is led inward toward the truth. Confidence low; flagged as new term.

'The Good Savior' — standard Manichaean Christological epithet (ⲥⲏⲣ being Lyc. contraction of σωτήρ). The dominical saying that follows alludes to Matthew 10:42 ('whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is a disciple, he will by no means lose his reward').

'These little believers' — direct allusion to Matt 10:42 μικροί. Mani then glosses on line 21: 'The Savior calls the holy one a little believer' — i.e., the apostolic 'little ones' are the elect/holy ones. Mani extends the principle to catechumens (line 22+).

Tentatively rendered 'they busy themselves with' / 'they are absorbed in.' The form may relate to ⲣ̄-ⲃⲗⲗⲉ 'be busy/preoccupied with' or to a Lyc. variant. Pairs syntactically with ⲥⲉⲃⲓⲣⲁⲩϣ 'they are anxious' (line 27) as a doublet of worldly preoccupation. Confidence low; flagged as new term.

Lycopolitan plural forms of ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' and ⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'kingship/kingdom'; ⲣⲁⲓ̈ is the Lyc. plural marker. Translated 'kingships' to preserve the abstract-political register of the four-kingdoms doctrine.

'The Holy Spirit' (πνεῦμα ἅγιον). Standard nomen sacrum abbreviation. The believing catechumen and the righteous believer are characterized as those in whom the Holy Spirit indwells — a key Manichaean ecclesiological doctrine of pneumatic indwelling parallel to the Mind of Light's residence in the elect.

Translated 'their (hearts/lips)' tentatively. The form ϩⲧⲏⲩ is unusual; in context (placing X to speak the truth in one heart) it must denote a faculty of speech or seat of intention. Possibly Lyc plural of ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' or related to a body-part for speaking. The transcription [2] follows the page's convention where 2 = ϩ; here the bracket marks the ϩ as editorially restored.
Translated 'which is divided' from ⲡⲱⲣⲭ/ⲡⲱⲣϫ 'separate, divide' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). Sense uncertain in this fragmentary line.
